subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: Is current source evidence enough to treat this early-call clipping as fixed, or should maintainers require a fresh live Twilio/OpenAI reproduction before authorizing code changes?
rationale: The current implementation has plausible improvements, but no live audio artifact or diagnostics tie those changes to this symptom, and the remaining hypotheses span provider format, output gain, and pacing.

options.title: Require live diagnosis first
options.body: Keep this open until a maintainer or reporter supplies redacted Twilio/OpenAI call audio or level/queue diagnostics that localize the clipping before a fix is attempted.

options.title: Queue instrumentation only
options.body: Allow a narrow diagnostics PR that records safe peak-level, frame, and queue stats without changing audio behavior yet.

options.title: Close as likely fixed
options.body: Treat the current PCMU/resampler/pacer state as sufficient, accepting the risk that the reported live symptom was never rechecked.

recommendation.title: Require live diagnosis first
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a maintainer or reporter supplies redacted Twilio/OpenAI call audio or level/queue diagnostics that localize the clipping before a fix is attempted.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored recent realtime setup hardening and is a strong routing candidate for deciding whether source evidence or live telephony proof is enough here.
